external_entities.name: developer
external_entities.description: A person who writes changes, pushes branches, and may manually start a rebuild of main.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server
external_entities.notes: The source does not state where developers are located.

external_entities.name: public package registry
external_entities.description: The public package registry reached during dependency resolution.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet

processes.name: git server
processes.description: The self-hosted git server containing developer branches and the source used for builds.
processes.source_excerpt: our self-hosted git server, which sits on the corporate network

processes.name: build runner
processes.description: The runner that fetches source, resolves the dependency lockfile, produces container images, pushes images, calls the deploy controller, and can manually rebuild main.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.
processes.notes: A shared build token is used to call the deploy controller. The source also states that any developer can log in to the build runner.

processes.name: deploy controller
processes.description: The controller that records which image SHA the estate should use and answers store server release queries.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network and holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on.
processes.notes: The runner's token is a shared build token, the same for every pipeline, and has not been rotated since setup.

processes.name: store server
processes.description: A small server in each store's back office running the till software as a container; it polls for the current release, pulls changed images, and restarts the container.
processes.source_excerpt: Each store has a small server in the back office running the till software as a container.
processes.notes: The source describes about 1,200 stores but does not identify each server separately.

data_stores.name: image registry
data_stores.description: The registry in the build environment where finished container images are stored; images are tagged with the commit SHA and pulled by store servers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry, which is also in the build environment.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the image registry encrypts what it stores.

data_flows.name: push branches
data_flows.description: A developer pushes a branch to the self-hosted git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

data_flows.name: merge trigger
data_flows.description: A merge to main starts a build that the build runner picks up.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A merge to `main` is what starts a build.
data_flows.notes: The source does not specify the trigger mechanism or protocol.

data_flows.name: fetch source
data_flows.description: The build runner fetches source from the git server after picking up a merge.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source

data_flows.name: resolve dependencies
data_flows.description: The build runner reaches out to the public package registry while resolving the dependency lockfile.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_flows.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.
data_flows.data_description: Dependencies downloaded according to the lockfile

data_flows.name: push image
data_flows.description: The build runner pushes the finished container image to the image registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_flows.notes: Images are tagged with the commit SHA.
data_flows.data_description: Finished container image tagged with the commit SHA

data_flows.name: request release
data_flows.description: The build runner asks the deploy controller to make an image the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When the image is pushed the runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release.
data_flows.notes: The runner uses a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since setup.

data_flows.name: kick off rebuild
data_flows.description: A developer logs in to the build runner and manually starts a rebuild of main.
data_flows.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
data_flows.notes: This path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

data_flows.name: poll release
data_flows.description: Each store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.notes: The source does not state what a store server presents to the controller.

data_flows.name: pull image
data_flows.description: A store server pulls the current image from the image registry when its running image differs from the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: if it differs from what it is running it pulls that image from the registry
data_flows.notes: The registry allows the pull, but nobody has written down what a store server presents to it.
data_flows.data_description: Container image for the current release

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network containing the self-hosted git server and deploy controller.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: which sits on the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: build environment
trust_boundaries.description: The separate environment containing the build runner and image registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The runner lives in its own build environment, separate from the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: store estate
trust_boundaries.description: The estate of about 1,200 stores containing the store servers.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The image registry is reachable from the store estate over the WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public internet reached by dependency resolution.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the public package registry on the internet

assumptions.assumption: The developer is assigned to the corporate network boundary because the source does not state a separate developer location and the developer interacts with the corporate git server.
assumptions.basis: The source says developers push branches to the self-hosted git server on the corporate network, but does not state where the developers are located.
